title: Urban Green Spaces
source: IELTop original sample content, released with the app. Replace with licensed material.
body: Many cities now treat parks as essential infrastructure rather than decoration. Research suggests that access to green space is linked to lower stress and better concentration. Planners who once measured success by road capacity increasingly measure it by how quickly a resident can reach a park on foot. This shift has practical consequences: a new park may be approved not because it is cheap, but because it serves a dense neighbourhood that lacks open air. Some councils go further and require developers to fund green space whenever they build housing above a certain size.

questions.prompt: How do some planners now measure success?

options.text: By walking distance to a park

questions.prompt: What is green space linked to in the passage?
What may councils require of developers?

options.text: To fund green space for larger housing projects
To limit the number of residents
